questions.q: What does terraform state list show?
options: The full attribute values of every resource
Every resource address currently tracked in state
A history of every past terraform apply
The contents of the .tf configuration files
questions.explain: terraform state list prints the address of every resource currently tracked in state, without showing their full attributes.

questions.q: Does terraform state rm destroy the real resource in Azure or AWS?
options: Yes, it immediately deletes the resource
No -- it only stops Terraform from tracking the resource; the real resource keeps running untouched
It destroys the resource only if it's an S3 bucket
It renames the resource in the cloud provider's console
questions.explain: terraform state rm is a state-only operation. It never calls a cloud provider API, so the real resource is left completely untouched.

questions.q: When would you use terraform state mv?
options: To physically move a VM from one Azure region to another
To rename a resource's address inside state, such as after refactoring local names, without touching real infrastructure
To migrate state from one backend to another
To move a resource from Azure to AWS
questions.explain: terraform state mv updates the resource's address inside state only -- useful when renaming local names or restructuring configuration into modules.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what is the FIRST thing to check if a state file looks lost or corrupted?
options: Immediately start re-importing every resource one by one
The automatic terraform.tfstate.backup file, written before most state-changing operations
Delete the backend configuration and start over
Contact the cloud provider's support line
questions.explain: The recovery order starts with the simplest option: the automatic local backup Terraform writes before most state-changing operations, before resorting to backend history or re-importing.

questions.q: Why is re-importing resources described as a 'last resort' for state recovery?
options: Because terraform import is deprecated
Because it is slow and manual, done resource by resource, compared to restoring a backup or a prior backend version all at once
Because it permanently destroys the real infrastructure
Because it only works for Azure resources
questions.explain: Re-importing rebuilds state one resource at a time by hand, which is far slower than restoring an automatic backup or a previous version from the backend's own history.
